evals.prompt: I inherited key_handler.py (attached) from a teammate and it's a nightmare to test. Every test has to fake stdin, a config file on disk, and stdout — and the actual logic (validating mouse/keyboard state, encoding keystrokes, applying settings) is buried between IO calls. Please restructure the module so the real logic is testable without touching stdin, files, or stdout, and write tests for that logic. Keep the external stdin->stdout behavior of handle_input() the same. Run the tests to confirm they pass.
evals.expected_output: A refactored key_handler module with IO pushed to the edges and the encoding/validation logic extracted as a pure, testable core, plus a passing test suite for that logic. External stdin->stdout behavior preserved.
expectations: The refactored module separates IO from logic: the encoding/validation logic is callable without stdin, files, or stdout (pure functions/classes take values rather than reading from sys.stdin or opening files).
Tests cover the functional core at least for: mouse-state validation (negative coordinates rejected), keyboard-state validation (empty key rejected), and key encoding (prefix plus modifiers).
Settings/config are passed into the logic as values rather than read from a file inside the tested code.
The external stdin->stdout behavior of the entry point is preserved (forwarded mouse input produces the same encoded output; non-forwarded input produces no output).
The tests pass when run (test_run.txt shows a passing run).

evals.prompt: Attached is register.py — our user-registration workflow with a four-variant error union and a retry helper. Write a thorough test suite for it. Specifically: cover every error variant of RegisterUserError (asserting each one's payload, not just 'it failed'), prove that a failed step short-circuits the rest of the workflow (later steps must not run), and test try_with_retry deterministically — no real sleeping, assert the exact list of attempts. Run the tests to confirm they pass.
evals.expected_output: A test suite covering all four error variants with payload assertions, short-circuiting of the workflow after a failed step, and a deterministic retry test asserting the exact attempt list. Tests pass.
expectations: Tests cover every error variant of RegisterUserError — InvalidCreateUser, EmailTaken, UserStoreUnavailable, PublishFailed — at least one test per variant.
Error-variant tests assert the payload (reason/email/cause), not just that an error was returned.
A short-circuit test proves later workflow steps do not run after an early failure (e.g. the publisher or store is not invoked when a previous step failed).
The retry test is deterministic: an injected operation with zero delay, asserting the exact attempt list.
The tests pass when run (test_run.txt shows a passing run).

evals.prompt: We need a small module that renders our server config (a nested dict: server name, port, listeners, and routes with methods and handlers) into a stable, human-readable text format. The output is complex enough that hand-writing assertions is painful, and we want this tested properly from day one. Build the module and its tests so the rendering logic is pure and testable, input is validated once at the boundary, and the complex output is verified with a golden-file test. Run the tests to confirm they pass.
evals.expected_output: A config-rendering module with pure rendering logic, input validated once at the boundary, tests using a golden file (committed expected output) rather than brittle hand-written assertions, and a passing test suite.
expectations: The rendering logic is pure: the core render function takes a config value and returns text with no IO inside it.
Input validation happens once at the boundary: a malformed config is rejected by a dedicated validation step, and validated domain values flow inward.

Complex output is verified with a golden-file test: committed expected output is compared against renderer output (with a documented update mechanism), rather than brittle hand-written per-line assertions.
The tests pass when run (test_run.txt shows a passing run).
